title: Galaxy Clusters and Gravitational Lenses
objective: After this level you can describe galaxy clusters and how their gravity bends light.
summary: Galaxies gather in clusters of hundreds or thousands. Their gravity bends light, magnifying galaxies behind them.

cards.headline: Some of the universe’s best telescopes are made of gravity.
Cities of galaxies
cards.body: Galaxies aren’t spread evenly. Many are gathered into clusters of hundreds or thousands of galaxies, bound together by gravity, much of it from dark matter.

cards.headline: Bending light
cards.body: Einstein’s relativity predicts that mass bends light. A massive galaxy cluster bends and magnifies the light of galaxies far behind it, acting as a natural lens. Webb’s first deep-field image, released in 2022, used exactly this trick to reveal much more distant galaxies.

questions.prompt: How did Webb’s first deep-field image see such distant galaxies?

options.label: A foreground galaxy cluster magnified their light
It used radio waves instead of infrared
It took pictures from two sides of the galaxy

questions.explanation: A galaxy cluster in the foreground acted as a gravitational lens, magnifying far more distant galaxies.

questions.prompt: From Level 85: what supplies much of the gravity holding galaxy clusters together?

options.label: Hot stars in the clusters
options.rationale: Stars are only a small part of the mass.

options.label: Black holes at every galaxy’s center
options.rationale: Their mass is small compared with the cluster.

questions.explanation: Much of a cluster’s mass, and so its gravity, is dark matter, which outweighs ordinary matter about five to one.
